question.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (\frac{3}{2}F)$ for the vector field $F$ where

$$
F={x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)\,i+x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)\,j-x{z}^{4}\,k.
$$
question.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{3}{2}F)=\frac{3}{2}∇\cdot F.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y))+\frac{∂}{∂z}(-x{z}^{4}) \\  & =2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)-4x{z}^{3} \\  & =4x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)-4x{z}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (\frac{3}{2}F) & =\frac{3}{2}∇\cdot F \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot (4x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)-4x{z}^{3}) \\  & =6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)-6x{z}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
